title: Leather
body_html:
Leather
Explore different types of leather and learn how material composition, thickness, surface finish, and treatment affect laser cutting and engraving results.
PU Leather
Synthetic leather commonly used for personalized accessories, patches, bags, wallets, and crafts.
Genuine Leather
Natural leather with variations in grain, thickness, tanning, and surface characteristics.
Synthetic / Faux Leather
Man-made leather alternatives available in a wide range of colors, textures, and finishes.
Suede
Leather or leather-like materials with a soft, napped surface that requires careful processing.
Leatherette
Leather-like sheet materials designed to reproduce the appearance and texture of natural leather.
Specialty Leather
Specialty leather and leather-like materials with unique colors, textures, coatings, or finishes.
Leather Materials
Leather materials vary significantly in composition, surface treatment, thickness, and laser response. Always identify the material before processing.
PU Leather
A polyurethane-based synthetic leather available in many colors, textures, and surface finishes.
Genuine Leather
Natural leather whose processing behavior can vary with tanning method, thickness, and surface finish.
Synthetic / Faux Leather
Man-made alternatives to natural leather. Check the polymer composition before laser processing.
Suede
Soft, napped leather or leather-like material that may require different settings from smooth leather.
Leatherette
Leather-like materials designed to imitate the appearance and texture of genuine leather.
Specialty Leather
Leather materials with special coatings, textures, finishes, colors, or other surface treatments.
Material Selection
Learn how to identify leather materials, compare different leather types, and select materials suitable for laser processing.

Laser Cutting
Learn how to prepare leather, select suitable processing conditions, and achieve clean and consistent cutting results.
Leather Laser Cutting Best Practices
Practical recommendations for cutting leather and leather-like materials with a laser.
Leather Cutting Troubleshooting

Laser Engraving
Learn how laser power, speed, focus, material surface, and leather type affect engraving depth and contrast.
Leather Laser Engraving Best Practices
Recommended practices for achieving clean, detailed, and consistent leather engraving.
Leather Laser Engraving Troubleshooting
Troubleshoot low contrast, excessive darkening, uneven engraving, smoke marks, and surface damage.
Material Safety
Not all leather-like materials are suitable for laser processing. Always verify the material composition before processing. Avoid materials containing chlorine or other substances that may produce hazardous fumes or damage laser equipment.
